`(Z, z0) → (Y, y0)` has a unique morphism `(X, x0) → (Z, z0)`.

property (being a terminal object) in the category of pointed covering spaces over `Y`.

def SerreCubeBoundary {n : ℕ} (t : SerreCube n) : Prop :=

    (∀ t, H (serreOne, t) = b.map t) ∧

theorem fundamental_group_amalgamation_universal_property
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [PathConnectedSpace X]
    (hlocal :
      ∀ (x : X) (W : Set X), IsOpen W → x ∈ W →
        ∃ V : Set X, IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ V ⊆ W ∧
          IsPathConnected V ∧

    {ι : Type*} (U : ι → Set X)
    (hopen : ∀ a, IsOpen (U a))
    (hcover : (⋃ a, U a) = Set.univ)
    (hconnected : ∀ a, IsPathConnected (U a))
    (hintersections : ∀ a b, IsPathConnected (U a ∩ U b))
    (x₀ : X) (hx₀ : ∀ a, x₀ ∈ U a)
    (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (f : ∀ a, Path (⟨x₀, hx₀ a⟩ : U a) ⟨x₀, hx₀ a⟩ → G)
    (f_homotopy :
      ∀ a (p q : Path (⟨x₀, hx₀ a⟩ : U a) ⟨x₀, hx₀ a⟩),

    (f_identity :

    (f_composition :

      F (Path.refl x₀) = 1 ∧

      (∀ (a : ι) (p : Path (⟨x₀, hx₀ a⟩ : U a) ⟨x₀, hx₀ a⟩),

nl: Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\overline{X}=X \cup \{\infty\}$. Declare a set $U \subseteq \overline{X}$ to be open if either $U$ is open in $X$, or $U=\{\infty\} \cup (X \setminus C)$ for some compact $C \subseteq X$. Prove that this defines a topology on $\overline{X}$ (the one-point compactification of $X$).

import Mathlib

/-- The one-point compactification: the described family of sets is a topology on
`X ∪ {∞}`. Hausdorffness is assumed, as is standard: compact sets are then closed,
which makes the intersection of the two kinds of open sets open. -/
theorem onePoint_compactification_isTopology (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] :
    ∃ t : TopologicalSpace (OnePoint X), ∀ U : Set (OnePoint X),
      @IsOpen (OnePoint X) t U ↔
        ((∃ V : Set X, IsOpen V ∧ U = OnePoint.some '' V) ∨
          (∃ C : Set X, IsCompact C ∧ U = insert OnePoint.infty (OnePoint.some '' Cᶜ))) := by
  sorry
